dataset: Wide-area LOLA south-polar DEM (far horizon tier)

source.label: LOLA 80 m/pix south polar DEM, LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ (80 S to the pole)
source.citation: Barker et al. 2023, Planet. Sci. J. 4, 183
source.coverage: 80 S to the south pole (stereographic radius ~304 km)

dem.crs_wkt: PROJCS["Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric / South Polar",GEOGCS["Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric",DATUM["Moon (2015) - Sphere",SPHEROID["Moon (2015) - Sphere",1737400,0,AUTHORITY["IAU","30100"]],AUTHORITY["IAU","30100"]],PRIMEM["Reference Meridian",0,AUTHORITY["IAU","30100"]],UNIT["degree",0.0174532925199433,AUTHORITY["EPSG","9122"]],AUTHORITY["IAU","30100"]],PROJECTION["Polar_Stereographic"],PARAMETER["latitude_of_origin",-90],PARAMETER["central_meridian",0],PARAMETER["false_easting",0],PARAMETER["false_northing",0],UNIT["metre",1,AUTHORITY["EPSG","9001"]],AXIS["Easting",NORTH],AXIS["Northing",NORTH],AUTHORITY["IAU","30135"]]

height.convention: metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere

limitations.resolution: 80 m/pixel, so the far tier resolves hills, crater rims and massifs hundreds of metres across, not boulders or the landing ellipse.
limitations.range: The ray-march stops at 150 km. Terrain beyond that can still block a body at the horizon, but at these sites its elevation angle is below the near-field skyline.
limitations.datum: Heights are metres above the 1737.4 km sphere (the Moon has no geoid). The file's height convention is detected from the data and recorded in `height`.
limitations.two_tiers: The mask takes the maximum of the 5 m near tier (to the site DEM edge) and this 80 m far tier (to 150 km). A coarser grid can miss a narrow ridge, so the far tier is a lower bound on obstruction beyond ~8 km, not an exact skyline.
limitations.scope: Terrain obstruction only; no power, communications, thermal or hazard meaning.
